e-6775.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Horizontal Hyperbola
e-6775.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $\dfrac{(x-1)^2}{9} - \dfrac{(y-2)^2}{4} = 1 ?$
e-6775.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\dfrac{(x-h)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(y-k)^2}{b^2}=1.
$$

In this case, we have $h = 1$ and $k = 2.$

Therefore, the center of the hyperbola is $(1,2).$

e-6776.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Vertical Hyperbola
e-6776.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $\dfrac{(y+3)^2}{16} - \dfrac{(x-1)^2}{9} = 1 ?$
e-6776.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\dfrac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{b^2}=1.
$$

Note that the given equation can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\dfrac{(y-(-3))^2}{16} - \dfrac{(x-1)^2}{9}=1
$$

In this case, we have $h = 1$ and $k=-3.$

Therefore, the center of the hyperbola is $(1,-3).$

e-5354.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Vertical Hyperbola Given an Equation in Expanded Form
e-5354.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$4 y^2  - 10 x^2 - 8 y  - 40 x  = 76?$
e-5354.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\dfrac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{b^2}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}-10{x}^{2}-8y-40x & =76 \\ 4{y}^{2}-8y-10{x}^{2}-40x & =76 \\ 4[{y}^{2}-2y]-10[{x}^{2}+4x] & =76 \\ 4[(y-1)^{2}-1]-10[(x+2)^{2}-4] & =76 \\ 4(y-1)^{2}-4-10(x+2)^{2}+40 & =76 \\ 4(y-1)^{2}-10(x+2)^{2} & =76-40+4 \\ 4(y-1)^{2}-10(x+2)^{2} & =40 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{10}-\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center is $(-2,1)$.

$$

$$

$$

after.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$3{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}-18x+8y=-13?$
after.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}-18x+8y & =-13 \\ 3{x}^{2}-18x-2{y}^{2}+8y & =-13 \\ 3[{x}^{2}-6x]-2[{y}^{2}-4y] & =-13 \\ 3[(x-3)^{2}-9]-2[(y-2)^{2}-4] & =-13 \\ 3(x-3)^{2}-27-2(y-2)^{2}+8 & =-13 \\ 3(x-3)^{2}-2(y-2)^{2} & =-13+27-8 \\ 3(x-3)^{2}-2(y-2)^{2} & =6 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{2}-\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{3} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center is $(3,2).$

content.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+20x & =-10 \\ 5{x}^{2}+20x-2{y}^{2} & =-10 \\ 5[{x}^{2}+4x]-2{y}^{2} & =-10 \\ 5[(x+2)^{2}-4]-2{y}^{2} & =-10 \\ 5(x+2)^{2}-20-2{y}^{2} & =-10 \\ 5(x+2)^{2}-2{y}^{2} & =10 \\ \frac{(x+2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{5} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center is $(-2,0).$

after.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$-3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-24x+8y=41?$
after.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-24x+8y & =41 \\ {y}^{2}+8y-3{x}^{2}-24x & =41 \\ [{y}^{2}+8y]-3[{x}^{2}+8x] & =41 \\ [(y+4)^{2}-16]-3[(x+4)^{2}-16] & =41 \\ (y+4)^{2}-16-3(x+4)^{2}+48 & =41 \\ (y+4)^{2}-3(x+4)^{2} & =41+16-48 \\ (y+4)^{2}-3(x+4)^{2} & =9 \\ \frac{(y+4)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(x+4)^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-(-4))^{2}}{{3}^{2}}-\frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(-4,-4).$
